A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Trust Region Masking work. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and the equations, tables, figures and reorganized sections support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 Section 7 reports original Qwen3-8B-Base training experiments on DAPO-MATH-17k, with AIME25 scores and training–rollout mismatch curves in Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v5 Section 5 retains original training and evaluation results in Figures 1–3, including revised results for the combined masking criterion.

M1.justification: The core TRM algorithm and SER procedure remain. Section 4.3 adds optional maximum-TV masking, and Appendix F changes LN-TRM's position weights to take the minimum over coupling and Pinsker bounds. LN-TRM and SER already existed in v2; they are not newly introduced methods.

E1.justification: Both versions train on deduplicated DAPO-MATH-17k and evaluate mathematical reasoning on AIME25 using Qwen3-8B-Base. No additional dataset, task, domain or experimentally tested mismatch scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Figures 1–3 retain their respective comparisons: Token IS versus PPO clipping; PPO versus TRM-Max and TRM-Avg; and loose individual criteria versus their combination. Figure 3 corrects the 0.002 legend from TRM-Max to TRM-Avg, matching v2's accompanying prose rather than introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the illustrative bound-evaluation settings from small/large KL divergence with cap comparisons to KL-only versus KL+TV information, specifying token TV 0.005 and sequence TV 0.05. The neural experiments retain the stated model, GRPO settings, learning rate, clipping and masking thresholds, evaluation sampling and avg@32 metric.

E4.justification: The numerical analysis shifts from the cap and divergence-regime comparisons in v2 Table 1 and Appendix C.5 toward KL/TV complementarity and their crossover. The numerical length-acceptance grid is removed, while its analytical length-bias argument remains. The empirical max/average/combined-criterion ablation retains its question and overall conclusion.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The avg@32 evaluation convention remains unchanged; the theoretical discussion of rejection probability does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are identical. Figure 3 replaces the combined-criterion curves: at the shared step 600, its plotted AIME25 score changes from approximately 0.212 to 0.239 under the retained stated settings, and reporting extends from about step 670 to 760. Table 1 adds TV-based numerical bounds, including 24.7 and 4.1, and removes large-divergence entries. Its old minimum labeled 'Adaptive' corresponds to the later 'Unified B*', not the standalone Adaptive row.

T1.justification: v5 substantially extends the retained KL theory with TV-based Pinsker-Marginal and Mixed bounds, a capped Coupling bound, and TV/hybrid Adaptive bounds with new derivations. Remark 2.1 corrects the constant relating the surrogate forms and specifies the baseline needed for value-level guarantees. New Appendix G derives an accepted/rejected-region guarantee with a support assumption, rejection penalty and distinct sample-ratio regime. Several foundational proofs are relocated rather than newly added.

C1.justification: v2 presents three tighter bounds and their minimum. v5 expands the central contribution to a KL/TV bound family and claims the tightest known guarantee across all divergence regimes. This broadens both the scope and comparative strength of the theoretical contribution, while retaining the central TRM and long-horizon motivation.

C2.justification: v2 Remark 6.2 uses high acceptance to justify approximate equality of masked and full surrogates. v5 Remark 4.3 explicitly rejects this inference and separates global-precondition validity from finite-sample robustness. Appendix G further explains that its reward-form value guarantee does not generally certify Algorithm 1's advantage-form stop-gradient update, and identifies the exponential cost of its precondition-free sample-ratio bound.

D1.justification: Implementation documentation becomes slightly less explicit: v2 separately specifies training and rollout batch sizes of 32, whereas v5 says only 'batch size 32'. Detailed LN-TRM/SER listings are condensed. Stored-logit computation, k2/k3 recommendations, total-batch normalization, and SER code and threshold range remain available.

R1.justification: The main positioning against classical trust-region methods and implementation mismatch remains. Several citations disappear, notably Qi et al. (2026) and its explicit attribution of an independently noted linear bound, and Yu et al. (2025), the cited source of the clipping settings. The revised Fang Liu reference retains the same arXiv identifier and represents an updated work rather than a new citation.

P1.justification: The paper is extensively rewritten and reorganized. Related work is integrated into the introduction, background explanations are compressed, token-level failure analysis joins the TRM section, and most main-text proofs move into reorganized appendices. The experiments, conclusion and length-neutral discussion are substantially condensed beyond changes required by the new scientific content.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially redesigned around bound routes and KL-only/KL+TV columns. The PPO clipping table, numerical length-acceptance grid and separate LN-TRM/SER algorithm panels disappear. Figures 1–2 are relocated with revised captions; Figure 3 is redrawn with changed axes and a corrected legend. The length-bias comparison table is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially improves the theoretical accuracy and scope of the paper. Remark 4.3 corrects v2's consequential claim that high acceptance makes masked and full objectives approximately interchangeable, while Remark 2.1 fixes the value-level surrogate normalization. The expanded bounds and Appendix G provide explicit derivations and clearer conditions. The new guarantee still does not establish monotonicity of Algorithm 1's general update, and its sample-ratio case has exponential cost; v5 now states these limits. These gains outweigh the modest loss of implementation and citation detail.
